name: AVM (AV2 reference encoder)
versionDocumented: AVM research-v15.0.0 (GitLab tag, commit 917ddae7db6d340b96246cf337b319dbd9cf98a7, 2026-05-06), whose option tables match GitHub tag v1.0.0, the AV2 v1.0.0 reference. Checked against the installed avmenc --help (AOMedia Project AV2 Encoder 15.0.0) built from that tag by scripts/install-encoders.sh. Options marked as not listed by --help are parsed by avmenc but missing from its help text.
summary: avmenc is the command-line encoder of AVM, the AOMedia Video Model that serves as the official reference software for the AV2 video standard. It exposes every AV2 coding tool as an on/off switch and reaches the highest compression of any AOMedia encoder (AOMedia cites roughly 30% savings over AV1), which makes it the right tool for archival experiments and for checking what AV2 can do. It is extremely slow (a reference implementation built for coding efficiency, not speed), has no two-pass mode, no container that ordinary players understand (raw OBU, IVF, or a provisional WebM 'V_AV2' track), cannot write HDR mastering-display or content-light metadata from the command line, and rejects 12-bit input in default builds (AV2 v1.0 has no 12-bit profile).
license: BSD 3-Clause Clear License plus the Alliance for Open Media Patent License 1.0

hdr.summary: AVM signals HDR only through the CICP fields in the sequence header: set --color-primaries=bt2020, --transfer-characteristics=smpte2084 (HDR10/PQ) or =hlg (HLG), and --matrix-coefficients=bt2020ncl, encode at --bit-depth=10, and set --chroma-sample-position=topleft as the AV2 common test conditions do for HDR. Full-range video is detected only from a Y4M header tag (COLORRANGE=FULL); there is no command-line range switch. avmenc has no flags for SMPTE ST 2086 mastering-display or MaxCLL/MaxFALL content-light metadata. The library defines metadata OBU types for them, but the application never inserts them, so HDR10 static metadata has to be added by a later tool or left out.
pitfalls: HLG is spelled 'hlg' in AVM's transfer enum. 'arib-std-b67' (the ffmpeg/x265 name) is rejected with a fatal 'Failed to set codec option' error.
Default builds accept only 8-bit and 10-bit (CONFIG_TESTONLY_12BIT_SUPPORT=0). 12-bit needs a test-only build and produces a non-standard profile.
There are no mastering-display or content-light-level options, so PQ output carries only CICP. Players fall back to their default tone-mapping assumptions.

The input bit depth comes from the Y4M header when one is present, and --input-bit-depth applies only to raw YUV. If the source is deeper than --bit-depth, the codec bit depth is raised to match, with a warning on stderr unless --quiet is set.
Without --obu or --ivf, and with an output name that does not end in .obu or .ivf, avmenc writes WebM with the provisional codec ID 'V_AV2', which most tools do not recognize.

The --qp scale is the 8-bit qindex scale and is shifted internally for 10-bit (24 per extra bit), so the same --qp gives similar quality at 8 and 10 bit. 10-bit also accepts negative values down to -48.

Leaving --chroma-sample-position at 'unspecified' is legal, but the CTC assumes co-located (top-left, Type 2) siting for HDR. Older CTC versions spelled this 'colocated', and that name is not in the v1.0.0 enum.
avmdec writes Y4M without a frame rate (F0:0). Tools that pair frames by time, such as FFmpeg's psnr filter, then compare the wrong frames; compare decoded frames by index.

presets.notes: Speed 0 is the best-efficiency setting, and all AV2 common-test-condition and verification encodes use it. Expect minutes per frame at 1080p and above on one thread.
Prunes a little search compared with 0. Speed features are enabled in steps at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Above speed 1 with no resize, the dynamic superblock size picks 128x128 instead of 256x256 for content larger than 480 lines, which also changes efficiency.
A reasonable compromise for archival tests on short clips.

presets.speed: moderate for a reference encoder, still far slower than libaom or SVT-AV1

presets.notes: This is the last level with its own speed features.
The good-quality usage treats 7, 8 and 9 as 6 (avmcx.h).

rateControl.notes: Fixed-quality mode used by the AV2 common test conditions (--qp gives the qindex directly). Add --use-fixed-qp-offsets=1 --deltaq-mode=0 --enable-tpl-model=0 for strictly fixed per-level QPs, as the CTC does. Left at defaults, the encoder adapts the QP per pyramid level and per block. M is 0, -48 or -96 for 8, 10 or 12 bit.
Targets the --qp quality level but caps the bitrate at --target-bitrate. The upstream test suites rarely exercise it.
One-pass variable bitrate with lookahead (--lag-in-frames). Two-pass is not available: --passes must be 1, and --minsection-pct/--maxsection-pct are ignored. The default target is 256 kbps.

Buffer-constrained constant bitrate. The buffer flags take effect only here, because VBR uses fixed large internal buffers. Usage is still good quality (there is no real-time usage in v1.0.0), so it is not a fast mode.
Forces qindex 0. The encoder also switches to lossless when the best and worst allowed q both resolve to 0, and TCQ is disabled automatically.

options.description: Prints the full option list grouped into Options, Encoder Global, Rate Control, Keyframe Placement and AV2 Specific sections, then exits.
options.notes: Several flags that the encoder parses are not printed by --help: --cq-level, --tile-width, --tile-height, --use-fixed-qp-offsets, --fixed-qp-offsets, --frame-hash and --use-per-plane-frame-hash.

options.description: Reads encoder tool settings from a key = value text file (see Sample.cfg in the repo) before the command-line options are applied.
options.notes: Only the first --cfg is honored. Keys use underscore names such as superblock_size and enable_cdef, which are not the dashed CLI names.

options.description: Turns on debug mode, which makes the output bitstream deterministic so that repeated runs can be compared byte for byte.

recommendations.why: The upstream CI encode checks use --debug so that md5 comparisons between builds are meaningful.

options.description: Names the output file. The extension picks the container when no format flag forces one: .ivf writes IVF, .obu writes a raw OBU stream, and anything else writes WebM in builds with WebM support.
options.lumora: Lumora passes '-o {out}' with an .obu file in a temp folder, then concatenates the segment OBU files for AV2.
options.notes: Encoding fails if no output is given.

options.description: Writes the encoder's reconstructed (decoded) frames to a raw file so they can be compared with the source without running a decoder.

options.values: short codec name; only 'av2' in AVM builds
options.description: Selects the encoder interface. AVM ships a single encoder, so this is effectively fixed to av2.
options.notes: The CTC scripts pass --codec=av2 explicitly.

options.description: Number of encoding passes. AVM has dropped two-pass encoding, so any value other than 1 is a fatal error.

recommendations.why: The CTC specifies single-pass encoding for all comparisons.

options.lumora: Always passed as --passes=1 because AVM has no second pass, so this only states what the encoder does; it also keeps an encode on a pipe working if a future build changes the default (libaom's two-pass default writes an empty file on a pipe).

options.description: Chooses which pass to run. With one-pass encoding, 0 and 1 behave the same.
options.notes: Kept for compatibility with aomenc.

options.description: Names the first-pass statistics file. It is inherited from aomenc and has no practical use while only one pass is allowed.
options.notes: Vestigial in v1.0.0.

options.description: Stops after n input frames.

recommendations.why: The CTC describes encoding the two closed GOPs of a random-access test in parallel, with --limit for the first and --skip for the second, then concatenating the two OBU files. For its test sequences this gives the same bitstream as a single encode.

options.notes: The CTC warns that encoding a still image with a larger --limit makes the encoder use a full sequence header. Use --limit=1 for stills.

options.description: Discards the first n input frames before encoding.

recommendations.why: Used with --limit to split one source into independently encoded closed-GOP chunks (CTC section 4.8).

options.description: Encodes only every n-th frame after the skipped frames. This is mainly for quick tests.
options.notes: 0 is rejected.

options.default: not stated (good quality is already the only usage)
options.description: Selects the good-quality usage profile. It is the only usage AVM v1.0.0 defines, so the flag changes nothing.
options.notes: After v1.0.0, GitHub main added a separate --rt (realtime deadline) flag. It is not in v1.0.0.

options.description: Suppresses the per-frame progress line and the automatic profile or bit-depth upgrade notices.
options.notes: Note that -q is quiet here, not quantizer.

options.description: Prints the full encoder configuration (tools, QP, speed, partition sizes) before encoding starts.

recommendations.why: The CTC encode script always logs the configuration with --verbose so that runs are reproducible.

options.notes: Useful for confirming that CICP values were accepted.

options.values: optional: 0 disable, 1 PSNR at input bit depth, 2 PSNR at stream bit depth
options.default: 2 when given without a value; off when absent
options.description: Adds PSNR to the status output. The optional value chooses whether PSNR is measured at the input or at the coded bit depth.

options.default: WebM is the default output when WebM IO is enabled (CONFIG_WEBM_IO=1 by default)
options.description: Forces WebM output even when the output name ends in .ivf or .obu.
options.notes: The track uses codec ID 'V_AV2'. Treat this as provisional: few demuxers or players recognize it. Fatal error if the build lacks WebM support.

options.description: Writes an IVF file (simple frame-indexed container, FourCC AV02).
options.notes: avmdec and analysis tools read IVF.

options.description: Writes a raw AV2 OBU stream with no container.

recommendations.why: The CTC requires .obu output and computes bitrate from the .obu file size.

options.lumora: Always passed. Lumora writes .obu segments and joins them by byte concatenation, since AV2 has no MP4 or Matroska binding yet.
options.notes: Concatenating closed-GOP OBU streams is the same method the CTC uses for parallel GOP encodes.

options.description: Prints a histogram of the quantizers chosen across the encode.
Prints a histogram of per-frame bitrates.
Hides the warnings that avmenc prints about settings it considers risky.
Still prints configuration warnings but does not stop to ask whether to continue. Use it for unattended runs.
options.lumora: Not passed. Lumora pipes Y4M on stdin, so an interactive warning prompt could stall an encode. Adding -y would be safer.

options.description: Decodes each frame inside the encoder and compares it with the encoder's reconstruction. 'fatal' stops on the first mismatch and 'warn' only reports it.
options.notes: Useful when experimenting with unusual tool combinations.

options.description: Declares raw input as YV12 (4:2:0 with V before U).
options.notes: Raw input only. Y4M headers override it.

options.description: Declares raw input as planar 4:2:0 YUV.
options.notes: Raw input only.

options.description: Declares raw input as planar 4:2:2. The profile is raised to the 4:2:2 profile automatically.
options.notes: Raw input only.

options.description: Declares raw input as planar 4:4:4. The profile is raised to the 4:4:4 profile automatically unless --monochrome is set.
options.notes: Raw input only.

options.description: Selects the encoder usage profile. v1.0.0 defines only good quality (0).
options.notes: Validation allows 0..1, but only one usage configuration table exists, so 1 most likely fails at initialization. Untested here.

options.description: Caps the number of worker threads. Threads only help when there are several tiles or row-based multithreading is on.

recommendations.why: The CTC verification configuration uses one thread and one tile to measure the best possible coding gain.

recommendations.value: match the tile count (e.g. 4 for 4 column tiles)
recommendations.why: For speed, the CTC pairs threads with tiles: two threads for two tiles and four for four.

options.lumora: Passed as --threads={threads} from Lumora's per-segment thread budget.
options.notes: Fatal error above 1 in builds without CONFIG_MULTITHREAD.

options.description: Sets the AV2 bitstream profile. avmenc raises it automatically when the input is 4:2:2 or 4:4:4, so it rarely needs setting by hand.
options.notes: The profile values come from the enum in av2/common/enums.h. A comment in avmenc.c calls profile 4 the 4:2:2 profile, which contradicts that enum. All defined profiles are 10-bit maximum.

options.description: Frame width. Needed for raw YUV input. Y4M input supplies it.
Frame height. Needed for raw YUV input.
options.notes: -h means height, not help. Use --help for help.

options.description: Writes a larger maximum frame width into the sequence header, so that a stream can later switch to bigger frames without a new sequence header.
options.notes: Spelled with underscores, unlike almost every other flag.

options.description: The height counterpart of --forced_max_frame_width.
options.notes: Spelled with underscores.

options.description: Tags WebM output with a stereoscopic 3D layout. The coded video is not changed.
options.notes: Only present in builds with WebM IO, and only affects WebM output.

options.description: Sets the precision of output timestamps in fractional seconds.
options.notes: Validation requires den between 1 and 1e9 and num no greater than den. In v1.0.0, avmenc sets the timebase to 1/1000 before parsing, then replaces it with the inverse frame rate (from --fps or the input file) after all options are parsed, so a value given with --timebase appears to be overwritten. This comes from reading apps/avmenc.c and has not been tested.

options.description: Overrides the stream frame rate. Rate control and timing info use it.

effect.quality: affects rate control in bitrate modes

options.notes: Must be positive.

options.description: Turns on error-resilient coding for all frames, limiting dependencies on earlier state so that a decoder can recover after packet loss.
options.notes: Not useful for file-based encodes.

options.description: Sets the internal coding bit depth. 10-bit improves gradients and is required for HDR. 12 is listed but rejected unless the build enables the test-only 12-bit profile.

recommendations.why: The CTC HDR class (BT.2100 PQ) is 10-bit, and 10 is the highest depth any defined AV2 profile supports.
The CTC encodes the synthetic gaming and animation class (B1) at 10-bit even when the source is 8-bit.

options.lumora: Passed as --bit-depth={bits} and always 10: Lumora offers AV2 at 10 bits only, because 12-bit is a test-only profile outside the AV2 v1.0 specification, and a standard build refuses it ('g_bit_depth out of range').
options.notes: The help says '8 for version <=1, 10 or 12 for version 2', which is inherited wording. If the input is deeper than this value, avmenc raises it to the input depth with a warning. 12-bit needs CONFIG_TESTONLY_12BIT_SUPPORT=1, which defaults to 0.

options.description: Declares the bit depth of raw YUV input. With Y4M input, the header's depth wins and this flag is ignored.
options.lumora: Passed as --input-bit-depth={bits}. Lumora feeds Y4M, so the Y4M header takes priority and the flag is harmless.

options.description: How many future frames the encoder may buffer for look-ahead decisions such as alt-ref placement, temporal filtering and the pyramid structure.

recommendations.why: The CTC random-access configuration uses --lag-in-frames=19.

options.notes: 0 gives a low-delay structure, as in the CTC LD configuration.

options.description: Encodes luma only and drops the chroma planes.
options.notes: With 4:4:4 input it stops the automatic 4:4:4 profile upgrade.

options.description: Uses the full sequence header instead of the reduced still-picture header for single-image encodes. 'hdr' here means header, not high dynamic range.
options.notes: Not an HDR option despite the name.

options.values: 0 off, 1 on for every frame, 2 on for key and altref frames
options.default: 1 (library default in encoder_usage_cfg; the help text says 2)
options.description: Turns on trellis-coded quantization, which picks quantized values along a state trellis so that the coefficients cost fewer bits.
options.notes: Sources disagree on the default: the help text says 2, but encoder_usage_cfg in av2_cx_iface.c initializes it to 1. TCQ is forced off when --enable-trellis-quant=0 or in lossless mode.

options.description: Emits a layer configuration record OBU describing the stream's layer structure, which matters for multi-layer and multi-stream AV2 streams.
Emits operating point set OBUs, which describe the decodable subsets of a layered stream.
How many operating point sets to write when they are enabled.
Emits an atlas segment OBU, which describes how several sub-pictures or streams are arranged into one composite picture.
options.notes: Part of AV2's multi-stream and composite video support.

options.description: Reads an ICC color profile and attaches it to the first frame as an ICC metadata OBU, for content whose color space CICP cannot describe.
options.notes: This is the only color-metadata attachment avmenc offers. There is no equivalent for HDR10 mastering or light-level metadata.

options.description: In buffer-constrained modes, lets the encoder skip frames when the buffer falls below this percentage.
options.notes: Not useful for file encodes.

options.values: 0 none, 1 fixed, 2 random, 3 dynamic, 4 CTC pattern, 5 bridge-frame test pattern
options.description: Allows coding frames at reduced resolution and scaling them back up after decoding, either at a fixed scale or decided by rate control.

effect.quality: - detail, but can help at very low bitrates

options.notes: Modes 2, 4 and 5 exist for testing. The values come from the RESIZE_MODE enum in encoder.h because the help gives none.

options.description: Scale factor for non-key frames when --resize-mode=1.
Scale factor for key frames when --resize-mode=1.
Selects the rate control mode: one-pass VBR, CBR, constrained quality (quality level with a bitrate cap), or constant QP.

recommendations.why: All CTC configurations use --end-usage=q with an explicit --qp.

options.lumora: Lumora always passes --end-usage=q and steers quality through --qp.

options.description: Target bitrate for VBR and CBR, and the bitrate cap in CQ mode.
options.notes: Ignored in Q mode.

options.description: Lowest allowed quantizer on the old 0-63 scale. It is mapped to a qindex and prints a deprecation warning.
options.notes: Use --min-qp instead.

options.description: Highest allowed quantizer on the old 0-63 scale, mapped to a qindex with a deprecation warning.
options.notes: Use --max-qp instead.

options.description: Lowest (best-quality) qindex that rate control may use.
options.notes: If min-qp and max-qp both resolve to 0, the encoder switches to lossless.

options.description: Highest (worst-quality) qindex that rate control may use.
options.notes: Also clamps --qp in Q mode.

options.description: How far below the target bitrate rate control may fall before correcting.
options.notes: Bitrate modes only.

options.description: How far above the target bitrate rate control may go before correcting.
options.notes: Bitrate modes only.

options.description: Decoder buffer size, in milliseconds of data, assumed by CBR rate control.
options.notes: VBR overrides it internally with 240000 ms.

options.description: Buffer fullness assumed at the start of playback, for CBR.
options.notes: VBR uses 60000 ms internally.

options.description: Buffer level that CBR rate control tries to maintain.
options.notes: VBR uses 60000 ms internally.

options.description: Two-pass VBR floor on per-GOP bitrate.
options.notes: Always ignored, because passes must be 1. avmenc warns that the option is ignored in one-pass mode.

options.description: Two-pass VBR ceiling on per-GOP bitrate.
options.notes: Always ignored, for the same reason as --minsection-pct.

options.description: Enables forward keyframes, which give an open-GOP structure where frames before a keyframe in display order may reference it.

recommendations.why: The CTC scripts default to closed GOPs (enable_open_gop: false in config.yaml, which VideoEncoder.py turns into --enable-fwd-kf=0). Closed GOPs keep chunks independently decodable and safe to concatenate.

options.notes: Keep it at 0 when encoding segments that will be concatenated.

options.description: Minimum spacing between automatically placed keyframes.

recommendations.why: The CTC random-access configuration uses fixed 65-frame GOPs (min = max = 65). All-intra uses 0 and 0.

options.notes: 65 is a test-harness choice. Longer intervals save bits on real content.

options.description: Maximum spacing between keyframes. 0 makes every frame a keyframe (all-intra).

recommendations.why: These are the CTC all-intra and low-delay settings.

options.notes: Lumora relies on the default. Every segment starts with a keyframe anyway.

options.description: Turns off automatic keyframe placement, so only the first frame is a keyframe.
options.notes: Hurts seeking.

options.description: Enables switch frames, which let a decoder switch between streams of different bitrate at that point without a full keyframe.
options.notes: Meant for adaptive-streaming ladders.

options.description: Interval between switch frames.
Controls how switch frames are inserted relative to the regular frame structure.
options.notes: The exact semantics of each mode are not documented in the help.

options.description: Chooses a regular switch frame or a random-access switch (RAS) frame.
options.notes: After v1.0.0, GitHub main added --sframe-conformance-option. It is not in v1.0.0.

options.description: Lets the encoder create hidden alternate reference frames (temporally filtered future frames) that later frames predict from.

recommendations.why: The CTC random-access configuration sets --auto-alt-ref=1.

options.values: path to an AVM grain table
options.description: Loads film grain synthesis parameters from a text table instead of estimating them. The decoder adds the described grain back on playback, so the encoder does not spend bits coding real grain.

effect.size: much smaller on grainy content when the source is denoised

recommendations.value: a measured filmgrn2 table, with a denoised source
recommendations.why: Grain synthesis encodes a compact parametric model and re-synthesizes it at the decoder instead of coding the noise itself.

options.lumora: Passed as --film-grain-table=<path> when film texture or the measured-grain option is on. Lumora writes the table in AVM's own 'filmgrn2' format (GrainTable, format .av2). Verified by encoding and decoding: the decoded grain matches the table's strength, and avmdec --skip-film-grain gives the clean picture back.
options.notes: The table format is defined in avm_dsp/grain_table.c (magic 'filmgrn2'). Its 'p' line has 13 values: AV1's 12, with the fifth renamed fgm_scale_from_channel0_flag, then block_size (0 = 16x16, 1 = 32x32). An AV1 'filmgrn1' table is accepted without an error message, but no grain is coded.

options.description: Sets the block size the decoder uses when laying synthesized grain over the picture.
options.lumora: Not passed. Lumora's grain tables set block_size 0 (16x16), this option's default.
options.notes: This is new in AV2. AV1 synthesis uses fixed 32x32 luma blocks.

options.values: 'ABxy': AB = operating point index, xy = level index (e.g. '0', '1021')
options.description: Asks the encoder to keep each operating point within a given AV2 level, constraining parameters such as bitrate and tile counts.
Path to the VMAF model used by the VMAF tuning modes.
options.notes: Only exists in builds configured with -DCONFIG_TUNE_VMAF=1, which defaults to 0. The README describes this build option.

options.values: built-in name (def, enh, asym, ts, ld) or a custom sub-GOP description string
options.description: Defines the reference structure and frame order inside each sub-GOP, either by naming a built-in preset or by spelling out a custom structure.

recommendations.why: The CTC low-delay configuration uses --subgop-config-str=ld with --lag-in-frames=0.

options.notes: The preset names come from subgop_config_str_preset_map in av2_cx_iface.c.

options.description: Same as --subgop-config-str, but reads the sub-GOP structure definitions from a file.
Adds show-existing-frame headers without order hints so that hidden frames are explicitly output.
options.notes: Bitstream-structure research option.

options.description: Adaptive quantization by segment: adjusts the quantizer per region based on variance or complexity, or refreshes regions cyclically for real-time use.

effect.quality: ± (can help flat areas, can lower PSNR)

options.notes: --deltaq-mode is the main block-level QP modulation in AVM. aq-mode is an older segment-based method.

options.description: Number of frames blended by the temporal filter when building alt-ref frames.

effect.quality: + denoised references; too high can smear motion

options.description: Strength of the temporal filter applied to alt-ref frames.
options.notes: Lower values keep more grain in the references.

options.default: adaptively chosen based on number of tiles
options.description: Chooses whether entropy-model averaging is done per frame or per tile.
options.notes: Only matters with --enable-avg-cdf=1.

options.description: Ties the CCSO filter signaling unit to the superblock size.

options.values: 0: no CDF update, 1: update on all frames, 2: selectively update
options.description: Controls how often the entropy coder adapts its probability tables between frames.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile
options.description: How often the encoder refreshes its coefficient bit-cost estimates during the RD search.
options.notes: Affects the encoder only, not the bitstream syntax.

options.description: Main speed/efficiency trade-off. Higher values prune more of the search. The good-quality usage treats 7-9 like 6.

recommendations.why: The CTC requires the best-performing setting (--cpu-used=0) for all configurations and comparisons.
6 is the fastest distinct level. 7-9 behave like 6 in good-quality usage.

options.lumora: Passed as --cpu-used={preset} with a default of 6, the fastest setting with its own speed features; the planner picks 5 or 4 only when the time budget allows. Speeds 7 to 9 are the same as 6.
options.notes: Even at 6, AVM is a reference encoder and remains very slow. A public test with the simple_encoder example took about 31 s per 320x180 frame at its defaults.

options.description: Bottom offset of the conformance cropping window, used when --enable-cropping-window=1.
Left offset of the cropping window.
Right offset of the cropping window.
Top offset of the cropping window.

options.values: 0: disable, 1: enable cross frame CDF init
options.description: Lets a frame start its entropy model from an earlier frame's adapted probabilities instead of the defaults.
Varies the quantizer per superblock, guided by the temporal dependency (TPL) model, toward better objective or perceptual quality.

recommendations.why: Every CTC configuration sets --deltaq-mode=0, together with fixed per-level QPs (--use-fixed-qp-offsets=1), so results are comparable across tests.

options.notes: Requires --enable-tpl-model. For normal use the default (1) is probably better, but that is an inference, not a measured claim.

options.description: Block size used by the noise estimator and denoiser that feed film grain synthesis.
options.notes: Present when CONFIG_DENOISE=1, which is the default.

options.description: Denoises the source before encoding and estimates film grain parameters from the removed noise. The decoder then re-adds synthetic grain of that strength.

effect.quality: + perceived on grainy content; - fidelity to exact grain

recommendations.why: Denoise-and-synthesize avoids spending bits on random grain. The same model underlies AV1 grain synthesis.

options.notes: Internally the value is divided by 10 before use. No upstream AVM guidance on specific strengths was found, so treat any number as a starting point. Present when CONFIG_DENOISE=1 (default).

options.description: Stops the in-loop filters at tile edges, which makes tiles fully independent at a small quality cost.

options.default: 1 (library default; the v1.0.0 help text says 0)
options.description: Turns off the machine-learning models that prune partition searches.
options.notes: Sources disagree. The v1.0.0 help says the default is 0, but default_extra_cfg in av2_cx_iface.c sets 1, and GitHub main has since changed the help text to say 1 is the default.

options.description: Turns off the machine-learning models that prune transform searches.
Number of decoded picture buffer slots the stream may use for references.
Enables adaptive motion-vector-difference resolution, which codes MV differences at a precision that adapts to the block.
options.notes: New AV2 tool.

options.description: Allows fine angle offsets on directional intra prediction modes.
Initializes entropy models from an average of frame or tile statistics rather than a single source.
Writes banding hint metadata so that a decoder or display can apply debanding where the encoder detected banding risk.

options.notes: Most valuable for smooth gradients in HDR and 8-bit content, but player support is unknown.

options.description: Enables block adaptive weighted prediction, which corrects brightness changes between reference and current blocks, as in fades and flicker.

options.values: 0: false, 1: true with regular decoder, 2: true with optimized decoder
options.description: Enables backward reference update, which lets a reference buffer be refreshed using later decoded content.
options.notes: Experimental option, off by default.

options.description: Enables cross-component sample offset, an in-loop filter that uses luma to correct chroma (and other component) errors.
options.notes: Wide-gamut content tends to show chroma errors more, so leave it on.

options.description: Enables a cross-chroma transform that decorrelates the Cb and Cr residuals before coding.
Enables the constrained directional enhancement filter, which removes ringing around edges.

options.values: 0: always off, 1: always on, 2: adaptive per frame
options.description: Controls whether CDEF also filters blocks that have no coded residual.
Enables chroma-from-luma intra prediction, which predicts chroma from the reconstructed luma texture.
Restricts chroma to the DCT only, skipping the other transform types.
Lets the encoder signal separate quantizer offsets for the chroma planes.
options.notes: Can help keep wide-gamut chroma clean, but no upstream guidance was found.

options.description: Signals a conformance cropping window, so the decoder outputs a smaller picture than the coded one (for example 1080 lines from a 1088-line coded frame).
options.notes: Set the four --crop-win-*-offset values with it.

options.description: Enables compound weighted prediction, which mixes two references with signaled, unequal weights.
Enables the deblocking filter that smooths block edges.
Enables difference-weighted compound prediction, which blends two references with a mask derived from their difference.

options.values: 0: no reorder, 1: reorder with constraints, 2: always reorder
options.description: Controls reordering of the dynamic reference MV candidate list so that likely candidates get cheaper indices.
Allows separate luma and chroma partition trees (semi-decoupled partitioning) on inter frames too.

recommendations.value: 0 (only in CTC ECF-6 screen RGB tests)
recommendations.why: The CTC extended-chroma-format screen content class turns it off alongside --tune-content=screen.

options.description: Enables AV2's extended partition shapes beyond quad, binary and the basic rectangles.
Allows more segmentation segments than the base count, for finer per-region parameter control.
Enables flexible motion vector resolution, choosing MV precision per block.
Enables the flipped ADST, identity and 1-D transform types in addition to plain DCT/ADST.
Enables forward skip coding, a residual mode that codes coefficients without a transform. It suits screen and synthetic content.
Enables the guided detail filter, an AV2 in-loop filter that restores detail lost to quantization.
Searches for frame-wide camera motion models such as pan, zoom and rotation, and uses them as prediction.
options.notes: Off by default in v1.0.0, unlike libaom AV1. Sample.cfg in the repo turns it on.

options.description: Uses a much larger motion search window so that very fast motion can be found.
options.notes: A plausible choice for sports or fast action, but not tested upstream in CTC.

options.description: Enables intra bi-prediction, which combines predictions from two directions.
When forward skip coding is off, still allows the identity transform for intra blocks.
options.notes: Only matters with --enable-fsc=0.

options.description: Enables implicit masked blending of compound predictions near picture boundaries and out-of-frame references.
Enables data-driven (trained) transforms for inter residuals.
Enables wedge-shaped masks that blend two inter predictions along a straight edge.
Enables blending an inter prediction with an intra prediction in one block.
Allows wedge masks for inter-intra blending.
Enables a secondary transform applied after the primary transform on inter blocks.
Enables intra block copy, which predicts a block from an already coded area of the same frame. Very effective for text and UI.
options.notes: On by default unless the build sets CONFIG_SHARP_SETTINGS.

options.values: 0: disable, 1: extend search to the local area, 2: only use the local search range
options.description: Controls the search range extension for intra block copy.

recommendations.why: The CTC uses --tune-content=screen --enable-intrabc-ext=1 for the screen-sharing class (B2).
The CTC uses 1 for most classes and 2 for the 640x360 and 480x270 classes (A4, A5).

options.description: Enables a data-driven (trained) intra prediction mode.
Smooths the reference edge pixels before directional intra prediction.
Enables the intra secondary transform.
Enables joint coding of the two motion-vector differences in compound prediction.

options.values: 0: no filter, 1: filter without overlay, 2: filter with overlay
options.description: Applies the temporal denoising filter to key frames, optionally followed by an overlay frame that restores the exact source.

recommendations.why: The CTC disables encoder-only pre-filtering, including key-frame filtering, in every configuration.

options.notes: For ordinary encodes the default is likely fine. The CTC value exists for comparability.

options.description: Also deblocks edges inside prediction blocks that are split into sub-blocks, for example by optical flow refinement.
Master switch for masked compound modes (wedge and difference-weighted).
Signals a multi-frame header OBU, which shares header information across several frames.
Enables multi-hypothesis cross-component prediction, an extension of chroma-from-luma.
Lets intra prediction use reference lines further from the block edge, not only the adjacent row and column.
Derives the sign of some MV differences instead of coding it.
Tracks motion trajectories across frames to build better temporal MV candidates.
Allows compound prediction from two references on the same temporal side, both past or both future.

options.values: 0: off, 1: switchable per block, 2: all blocks with simple compound average, 3: auto (switchable per frame by the encoder)
options.description: Enables optical-flow refinement of compound motion vectors at sub-block level, done by both encoder and decoder.
Allows coding overlay frames that correct filtered alt-ref frames back toward the source when they are shown.
Enables the Paeth intra predictor.
Enables palette mode, which codes blocks with a few distinct colors as indices into a small palette. Strong for screen content and flat cartoons.
Hides one coefficient sign or parity bit in the sum of the other coefficients, which saves bits.
Enables the pixel-classified Wiener mode of loop restoration.
options.notes: Needs --enable-restoration=1.

options.description: Enables quantization matrices, which quantize high frequencies more coarsely than low ones.
options.notes: Use with --qm-min/--qm-max.

options.description: Allows rectangular (non-square) block partitions.
Enables temporal motion vector prediction from the motion stored in reference frames.
Enables decoder-side motion vector refinement, where the decoder improves signaled MVs with a local search.
Keeps a bank of recently used motion vectors as extra MV candidates.
options.notes: GitHub main later ties this to switch-frame conformance.

options.description: Enables the loop restoration filter stage (Wiener variants).
Allows semi-decoupled luma and chroma partition trees on key frames.
Signals the reference refresh flags with 3 bits instead of 8 bits.
Allows explicitly signaled warp models with all six affine parameters.
Enables skip mode, a cheap compound mode with no residual and inferred references.
Enables smooth (gradient) blending for inter-intra prediction.
Enables the smooth intra predictors that interpolate gently across the block.
options.notes: Gradient-friendly modes matter for skies in HDR. Leave on.

options.values: 0: disable, 1: TIP frame used as reference or direct output, 2: TIP frame only used as reference
options.description: Enables temporal interpolated prediction, which builds an interpolated frame from two references along motion trajectories. That frame can serve as a reference or be output directly with almost no bits.
options.notes: One of AV2's headline tools.

options.description: Applies MV refinement and optical flow when building TIP frames.
options.notes: Only matters with TIP enabled.

options.description: Runs a temporal dependency model over the lookahead to find which blocks are referenced most, then spends more bits on them. Required for --deltaq-mode.

recommendations.why: The CTC sets --enable-tpl-model=0 with --use-fixed-qp-offsets=1 and --deltaq-mode=0, so the coded QPs are exactly as specified.

options.notes: Lumora leaves it at the default (on), which suits non-research encodes.

options.values: 0: no trellis, 1: all encoding stages, 2: only last encoding pass, 3: disable trellis in estimate_yrd_for_sb
options.description: Controls rate-distortion optimization of quantized coefficients and when it runs.
options.notes: Setting 0 forces --enable-tcq off to avoid an encoder/decoder mismatch.

options.description: Allows splitting a block's residual into several transform blocks.
Enables 1:2:4:1 and 1:4:2:1 four-way splits.
Enables warp prediction that derives its model from neighboring blocks' motion.
Allows explicitly signaled warp model adjustments.
Master switch for local warped (affine) motion prediction.
Lets a block extend a neighbor's warp model.
Enables the non-separable Wiener mode of loop restoration.

options.values: 0: off, 1: reuse co-located decision, 2 to 6: increasing aggressiveness
options.description: How aggressively the extended rectangular partition search is pruned.
Signals the reference-buffer mapping explicitly instead of letting the decoder derive it.
Applies one of 16 built-in film grain parameter sets. It exists for conformance testing.
options.notes: Not intended for real content.

options.description: Uses the video sequence header even when only one frame is encoded, instead of the still-picture form.
Turns on features that allow frames to be decoded in parallel, by disabling backward entropy adaptation between frames.

recommendations.why: The CTC encode scripts pass --frame-parallel=0.

options.description: Periodically gives selected frames extra quality.
options.notes: Mainly a real-time rate-control option.

options.description: Ties the guided detail filter's signaling unit to the superblock size.
Extra bit share for golden frames in CBR mode.
options.notes: CBR only.

options.description: Maximum depth of the hierarchical reference pyramid in a golden-frame group.

recommendations.why: The CTC random-access and low-delay configurations fix the pyramid at height 4 for a 16-frame sub-GOP.

options.description: Minimum pyramid depth in a golden-frame group.

recommendations.why: The CTC sets min and max pyramid height to 4.

options.values: unspecified, left, center, topleft, top, bottomleft, bottom
options.description: Signals where chroma samples sit relative to luma for 4:2:0 and 4:2:2. It also tells the Y4M reader how to interpret the input.

recommendations.why: The CTC adds --chroma-sample-position=topleft for HDR sequences, which assume co-located (Type 2) chroma.
The CTC states that BT.709 and other non-HDR video uses vertical chroma siting (Type 0, left).

options.lumora: Always passed as --chroma-sample-position=center because Lumora's 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 chroma is averaged over 2x2 (or 2x1) luma sites, so the chroma sample sits in the middle of them (H.273 type 1). AVM writes no siting for 4:4:4.
options.notes: Parsed both as a global and as a stream option. AVM's enum is richer than AV1's (adds center, top, bottomleft, bottom). CTC v7 and earlier used 'colocated', which is not a valid v1.0.0 value.

options.description: Declares horizontal chroma subsampling for the input.
options.notes: Normally inferred from Y4M or the --i42x flags.

options.description: Declares vertical chroma subsampling for the input.

options.values: bt709, unspecified, bt601, bt470m, bt470bg, smpte240, film, bt2020, xyz, smpte431, smpte432, ebu3213
options.description: Writes the CICP color primaries of the content into the sequence header. The pixels are not converted.

recommendations.why: This is the CTC HDR signaling for BT.2100 content.

options.lumora: Passed as --color-primaries={cp_name}: bt2020 for PQ and HLG, bt709 for SDR. Both names are valid AVM enum values.
options.notes: Use smpte432 for Display P3 content.

options.values: identity, bt709, unspecified, fcc73, bt470bg, bt601, smpte240, ycgco, bt2020ncl, bt2020cl, smpte2085, chromncl, chromcl, ictcp, ipt-c2, ycgco-re, ycgco-ro
options.description: Writes the CICP matrix coefficients (YUV conversion) into the sequence header.

recommendations.why: This is the CTC HDR signaling.

options.lumora: Passed as --matrix-coefficients={mc_name}: bt2020ncl for PQ and HLG, bt709 for SDR. Both are valid.
options.notes: AVM adds ipt-c2, ycgco-re and ycgco-ro to the AV1 list. 'identity' is used for RGB (4:4:4) coding.

options.values: unspecified, bt709, bt470m, bt470bg, bt601, smpte240, lin, log100, log100sq10, iec61966, bt1361, srgb, bt2020-10bit, bt2020-12bit, smpte2084, hlg, smpte428
options.description: Writes the CICP transfer function into the sequence header. This is the field that marks a stream as PQ (smpte2084) or HLG (hlg).

recommendations.why: The CTC HDR class uses smpte2084. 'hlg' is the spelling in AVM's transfer enum.

options.lumora: Passed as --transfer-characteristics={tc_name} with smpte2084 for PQ, hlg for HLG and bt709 for SDR. After every AV2 export Lumora reads the content interpretation OBU back (AV2Stream) and fails the export if the signaling is wrong.
options.notes: Enum matching is exact and case-sensitive.

options.description: Encodes mathematically lossless output by forcing quantizer index 0.
options.notes: Also disables TCQ.

options.description: Size of the block-vector candidate list for intra block copy.
Size of the dynamic reference MV candidate list per reference frame.
options.notes: GitHub main's help now says 2-6. Treat values above 6 as possibly invalid.

options.description: Longest allowed golden/alt-ref group.

effect.size: smaller with longer groups on static content

recommendations.why: The CTC fixes min and max GF interval at 16 (the sub-GOP size).

options.notes: Must not exceed the lookahead.

options.description: Caps the size of inter frames as a percentage of the average frame budget.
options.notes: Bitrate modes.

options.description: Caps the size of intra frames as a percentage of the average frame budget.
options.notes: Bitrate modes.

options.description: Limits how elongated prediction blocks may be.
Largest block size the partition search may use.
options.notes: Cannot be below --min-partition-size.

options.description: Maximum number of reference frames one frame may use.
Shortest allowed golden/alt-ref group.

recommendations.why: CTC value.

options.description: Smallest block size the partition search may use. At 4K and above, or at higher speed settings, the floor is raised to 8 automatically.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile
options.description: How often mode-cost estimates are refreshed during encoding.
options.notes: Encoder only.

options.description: Sets a sequence-header flag that requires AV1-style output, where hidden frames are shown through show-existing-frame headers.
Sizes tile groups to fit a network packet. It overrides --num-tile-groups.
options.notes: For packetized streaming only.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile, 3: Off
options.description: How often motion-vector cost estimates are refreshed.
options.notes: Encoder only.

options.description: Legacy temporal denoiser strength inherited from libvpx and libaom. AVM v1.0.0 accepts it but does not use it.
options.notes: In v1.0.0 the value is range-checked (0..6) and stored in the encoder's extra config, but nothing in av2/encoder reads it, so it has no effect.

options.description: Maximum number of tile groups per frame, which allows a frame to be split across several OBUs.
Number of operating points signaled in the sequence header for layered streams.
options.notes: GitHub main has narrowed the help range to 1-7.

options.default: 9 (library default DEFAULT_QM_LAST; the help text says 15)
options.description: Flattest quantization matrix level the encoder may use (15 is effectively flat).
options.notes: Needs --enable-qm=1. The help text claims a default of 15, but default_extra_cfg in av2_cx_iface.c initializes qm_max to DEFAULT_QM_LAST, which quant_common.h defines as 9.

options.default: 5 (library default DEFAULT_QM_FIRST; the help text says 8)
options.description: Steepest quantization matrix level the encoder may use. Lower values weight high frequencies more strongly.
options.notes: Needs --enable-qm=1. The help text claims a default of 8, but default_extra_cfg in av2_cx_iface.c initializes qm_min to DEFAULT_QM_FIRST, which quant_common.h defines as 5.

options.description: Quality level for Q and CQ modes, given directly as a qindex. Lower means higher quality. The value is on the 8-bit scale and shifted internally for higher bit depths.

recommendations.why: The lowest CTC random-access operating points are qindex 110 and 135. All-intra starts at 85 and stills at 60.
These are the upper CTC random-access operating points, the low-bitrate end of the tested range.

options.lumora: Passed as --qp={quality}. Lumora interpolates between qualityBest=80 and qualityWorst=200.
options.notes: In Q mode the value is clamped to [--min-qp, --max-qp]. With default adaptive offsets (no --use-fixed-qp-offsets), frames in the pyramid get different effective QPs around this anchor.

options.description: Uses an adaptive variant of the quantizer that adjusts rounding per block.
Limits the set of single and compound reference combinations searched and signaled.

options.values: 0: all allowed reference combinations, 1: one reference combination
options.description: Limits temporal MV projection to a single reference combination.
Uses a smaller set of transform partition patterns.
Restricts which transform types are searched. Higher values allow fewer types.
options.notes: The help gives no values. The 0..3 range is from the validation check.

options.description: Multithreads the encoder across superblock rows inside a tile.

recommendations.why: Every CTC tile and thread configuration passes --row-mt=0.

options.lumora: Always passed as --row-mt=1, so builds whose default is off keep row multithreading.
options.notes: GitHub main has since changed the default to 0 (off). On those builds, pass --row-mt=1 explicitly to keep the speedup.

options.description: Signals a flag saying whether scan-type (progressive or interlaced source) information is present.
Picks the luma downsampling filter used by chroma-from-luma prediction, or lets the encoder choose adaptively.
Asks the encoder to keep each frame's compression ratio above this value divided by 100, as required by level limits.

options.values: 32-bit mask; bit 0 = Main tier, 1 = High tier
options.description: Chooses Main or High tier for each of up to 32 operating points.
Biases the deblocking filter toward preserving sharp edges. Higher values filter less.
Threshold under which blocks are treated as static and skipped early.
options.notes: Legacy option. Leave at 0.

options.description: Superblock size. Dynamic picks 256x256 for content of 720 lines or more at speeds 0-1, and smaller sizes at lower resolutions or higher speeds.

effect.size: smaller with larger SB on high-res

options.notes: The dynamic rules are in encoder_utils.c. Above speed 1, dynamic uses at most 128x128.

options.description: Splits each frame into 2^n tile columns, which can be encoded and decoded in parallel.

recommendations.why: The CTC uses four column tiles at 4K and two at 1080p to cut test time.
The CTC verification configuration uses a single tile for the best coding gain.

options.notes: Lumora sets --threads but not tiles. Without tiles or --row-mt, extra threads do little.

options.description: Splits each frame into 2^n tile rows.

recommendations.why: The CTC low-delay configuration uses 2 rows x 4 columns with 8 threads for 1080p-class content.

options.description: Writes timing information into the bitstream: none, a constant frame rate, or a decoder model.
options.notes: The help notes that 'model' only works without hidden frames and super-resolution.

options.description: Tells the encoder the content type. 'screen' turns on screen-content tools such as palette and intra block copy decisions for every frame.

effect.size: much smaller on UI and text

recommendations.why: The CTC applies --tune-content=screen to the screen-sharing class (B2).
Gaming and animation (class B1) are encoded with default tuning in mandatory CTC runs. 'screen' is only an optional extra test for them.

options.lumora: Passed as --tune-content=screen for the Screen content type when no time plan is set.
options.notes: Without this flag the encoder still runs a per-frame screen-content detector.

options.values: psnr, ssim, vmaf_with_preprocessing, vmaf_without_preprocessing, vmaf, vmaf_neg
options.description: Chooses which distortion metric the RD decisions optimize.
options.notes: Builds without CONFIG_TUNE_VMAF (the default) accept only psnr and ssim. The vmaf names are listed but fail validation.

options.description: Restricts inter blocks to the DCT.
Restricts intra blocks to the DCT.
Uses only the mode-implied default transform for intra blocks, skipping the transform search.

options.values: 0: off, 1: prune rect, 2: prune split, 3: prune rect + split
options.description: Uses a machine-learning model to prune extended rectangular partition choices.
options.notes: The encoder_usage_cfg table lists 0 for this field, but default_extra_cfg, which command-line runs use, has 2.

options.description: Chooses between the grouped and the short metadata OBU syntax.
Gives one-pass VBR an assumed average complexity per macroblock, to help it spread bits when it has only lookahead.
options.notes: VBR only.

options.description: Old-scale quality level, mapped to a qindex (for example 63 maps to 255) with a deprecation warning.
options.notes: Parsed by avmenc but not printed by --help. Use --qp instead.

options.description: Gives explicit, possibly uneven, tile column widths instead of an even log2 split.
options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help. The units are not documented and are presumably superblocks.

options.description: Gives explicit tile row heights.
options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help.

options.description: Uses fixed QP offsets for each pyramid level, derived from --qp, instead of letting the encoder adapt them.

recommendations.why: Every CTC configuration sets --use-fixed-qp-offsets=1 so that QP per frame level is reproducible.

options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help. The arg_defs help text for this flag talks about comma-separated values, which really belong to --fixed-qp-offsets.

options.values: comma-separated offsets: keyframe, ALTREF, then internal alt-ref levels (at least 2 values)
options.description: Sets the QP offsets for each pyramid level by hand. Missing trailing values are filled in by halving.
options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help. Implies --use-fixed-qp-offsets=1. The help text says 5 offsets, while the code stores FIXED_QP_OFFSET_COUNT values.

options.description: Writes decoded-frame hash metadata OBUs so that a decoder can check its output. The hash covers the raw frame, the frame after film grain, or both.
options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help.

options.description: Writes separate hashes for Y, U and V instead of one per frame.
options.notes: Parsed but not listed by --help.

recipes.name: Best-efficiency random access (CTC-style)
recipes.why: This is the official AV2 random-access test configuration with the verification-test simplifications removed (speed 0, single tile). It shows the codec's full coding gain at an exactly controlled QP. Expect extremely long encode times.

recipes.name: HDR10 (PQ) 10-bit
recipes.why: This uses the CTC's HDR signaling with a 10-bit pipeline. The speed and tile choices trade some efficiency for a usable runtime. Mastering-display and MaxCLL metadata cannot be added by avmenc.

recipes.name: HLG 10-bit
recipes.why: This is the HLG variant. The transfer name must be 'hlg', the spelling in AVM's enum. The chroma siting follows the CTC's HDR convention, which the CTC defines for PQ. Applying it to HLG is an assumption.

recipes.name: Screen content / UI capture
recipes.why: These are the CTC settings for its screen-sharing class. Screen tuning forces palette and intra-block-copy decisions on every frame.

recipes.name: All-intra / still image
recipes.why: This is the CTC all-intra configuration. Use --limit=1 for single images so the encoder uses the reduced still-picture header.

recipes.name: Low delay
recipes.why: This adapts the CTC low-delay structure (no lookahead, forward-only references) for conferencing-style or latency-sensitive encodes. The speed is raised from the CTC's 0.

recipes.name: Parallel closed-GOP chunks
recipes.args: chunk A: --limit=65 ...; chunk B: --skip=65 --limit=65 ... (same settings, --enable-fwd-kf=0), then cat A.obu B.obu > full.obu
recipes.why: The CTC states that, for its test sequences, two closed-GOP chunks encoded separately and then concatenated give the same bitstream as one encode. This is the safe way to use many cores with a slow reference encoder, and it matches Lumora's segment-and-concatenate approach.

recipes.name: Film grain via table
recipes.why: Code a denoised source and let the decoder re-synthesize grain from a parametric table. The table must use AVM's 'filmgrn2' text format, not AV1's 'filmgrn1'.

recipes.name: Faster practical encode
recipes.why: Speed 6 is the fastest distinct level (7-9 behave the same). Tiles plus row multithreading give the threads work to do. Still far slower than libaom.

recipes.name: Lossless
recipes.why: Forces qindex 0 for bit-exact reconstruction. TCQ is disabled automatically.
